questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Monetary Policy Committee's first policy of FY 2026-27, announced on 8 April 2026:
1. The policy repo rate was kept unchanged at 5.25 per cent with a neutral stance.
2. The Marginal Standing Facility rate was kept below the repo rate, at 5.00 per cent.
3. The RBI projected FY27 CPI inflation at 4.6 per cent on the new CPI series, citing the West Asia conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruptions among the risks.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Standing Deposit Facility rate stayed at 5.00 per cent, below the repo rate, while the MSF rate and Bank Rate stayed at 5.50 per cent, above it. Statement 2 swaps the corridor: the MSF is the penal upper bound and the SDF the lower floor. The MPC is a statutory body under the RBI Act, 1934.
questions.s: Drishti IAS and 5paisa, 8 Apr 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the cancellation of the banking licence of Paytm Payments Bank in April 2026:
1. The Reserve Bank of India cancelled the licence under Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
2. A payments bank can accept deposits up to a per-customer limit but cannot lend.
3. The RBI said it would seek the winding up of the bank from the High Court.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The licence was cancelled with effect from the close of business on 24 April 2026 under Section 22(4) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, which governs licensing; Section 35A deals with directions to banks, which the RBI had used earlier when it barred fresh onboarding and then deposits. The RBI cited governance lapses and non-compliance with licence conditions.
questions.s: Business Today, Tribune and RBI, 24 Apr 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the export duty (windfall tax) on fuels revised by the Finance Ministry on 11 April 2026:
1. The export duty on diesel was raised to Rs 55.5 per litre and on aviation turbine fuel to Rs 42 per litre.
2. The export duty on petrol was kept at nil.
3. The stated aim was to earn more foreign exchange by encouraging exporters of refined fuels.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The earlier rates were Rs 21.5 per litre for diesel and Rs 29.5 for ATF since 26 March 2026. The purpose was the opposite of statement 3: to improve domestic availability during the West Asia war and stop exporters exploiting the gap between global and domestic prices.
questions.s: Outlook Business and News Arena India, 11 Apr 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana:
1. The Union Cabinet approved continuation of PMGSY-III until March 2028, and until March 2029 for bridges in hilly areas, with a revised outlay of Rs 83,977 crore.
2. The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj.
3. PMGSY was launched on 25 December 2000.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Cabinet extended PMGSY-III beyond March 2025, lifting the outlay by Rs 3,727 crore, and allowed 161 long-span bridges on sanctioned alignments. PMGSY is run by the Ministry of Rural Development, not Panchayati Raj, even though the roads serve villages.
questions.s: PM India and NBM&CW, 18 Apr 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about hydroelectric projects approved by the Union Cabinet in April 2026:
1. The 1,200 MW Kalai-II project is located in Anjaw district of Arunachal Pradesh.
2. Kalai-II is the first hydro project on the Subansiri river.
3. The 1,720 MW Kamala project is located in Anjaw district.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Kalai-II is the first hydro project in the Lohit basin (the Lohit is a tributary of the Brahmaputra), and is a joint venture of THDC India Ltd and the Arunachal Pradesh government. Kamala lies in the Kamle, Kra Daadi and Kurung Kumey districts, so both statements 2 and 3 fail.
questions.s: All India Radio and Punjab Kesari, Apr 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement signed on 27 April 2026:
1. The agreement entered into force on the day it was signed.
2. Dairy, animal and agricultural products were excluded from the agreement.
3. All Indian exports get duty-free access to New Zealand, which has indicated investment of up to 20 billion US dollars in India over 15 years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Negotiations concluded in December 2025 in about nine months, but the agreement must still be ratified by both countries before it enters into force. Keeping sensitive dairy and farm products out reflects India's protective stance for its farmers.
questions.s: All India Radio and Eximguru, 27 Apr 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the withdrawal of the United Arab Emirates from OPEC, announced on 28 April 2026:
1. The withdrawal from OPEC and OPEC+ took effect on 1 May 2026.
2. OPEC is headquartered in Vienna.
3. OPEC was founded in 1960 at Riyadh by Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and Venezuela.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The UAE cited a review of its production policy, restrictive quotas and a goal of lifting capacity to 5 million barrels per day by 2027. OPEC was founded in 1960 at Baghdad, not Riyadh; OPEC+ is the wider grouping that also includes Russia and other non-OPEC producers.
questions.s: All India Radio, Drishti IAS and Khaleej Times, 28 Apr 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (Amendment) Bill, 2025, passed by Parliament in the Budget Session that ended on 18 April 2026:
1. The Bill was passed in the Budget Session of 2026.
2. Under the Code, insolvency petitions of corporate debtors are adjudicated by the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India.
3. Its reported features include a creditor-initiated insolvency resolution process and frameworks for group and cross-border insolvency.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Code, enacted in 2016, is adjudicated for corporate debtors by the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), while the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) is the regulator, not an adjudicator. The 2025 Bill also replaces some criminal penalties with civil ones.
questions.s: All India Radio and PRS India, Apr 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Minimum Support Prices for kharif crops for the 2026-27 marketing season:
1. The MSP of common paddy was raised by Rs 72 to Rs 2,441 per quintal.
2. MSPs are approved by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs on the recommendation of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices.
3. Paddy received the steepest increase in MSP among the 14 kharif crops.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Cabinet raised the MSP of all 14 kharif crops in May 2026, and sunflower seed received the steepest increase, Rs 622 per quintal, so paddy's Rs 72 rise was modest. The announced prices are meant to give farmers at least 1.5 times the all-India weighted average cost of production.
questions.s: Deccan Chronicle, DT Next and Swarajya, May 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the RBI's surplus transfer to the Central Government for the accounting year 2025-26:
1. The record surplus of about Rs 2.86 lakh crore was approved by the Monetary Policy Committee.
2. The transfer is made under Section 47 of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, on the recommendation of the Central Board.
3. The previous highest transfer was about Rs 2.69 lakh crore, paid for 2024-25.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: On 22 May 2026 the RBI's Central Board approved the transfer, the highest dividend paid by the RBI to date. The MPC deals only with the policy rate under Section 45ZB, while the surplus is decided using the Economic Capital Framework by the Central Board.
questions.s: All India Radio and Outlook Business, 22 May 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's retail inflation data for April 2026, released on 12 May 2026:
1. All-India CPI inflation was 3.48 per cent, on the new base year of 2024=100.
2. The CPI is compiled by the Office of the Economic Adviser in the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade.
3. Food (CFPI) inflation, at 4.20 per cent, was higher than the headline figure.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The CPI is compiled by the National Statistics Office under MoSPI, which moved the base year from 2012 to 2024; it is the Wholesale Price Index that the Office of the Economic Adviser in DPIIT compiles. Rural inflation (3.74 per cent) was above urban (3.16 per cent).
questions.s: MoSPI and PIB, 12 May 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool launched on 12 May 2026:
1. The pool is administered by the New India Assurance Company.
2. It is administered by General Insurance Corporation of India (GIC Re) through a common underwriting committee of participating insurers.
3. The sovereign guarantee applies only to claims above USD 100 million after reserves and reinsurance are exhausted.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The pool insures Indian-flag, coastal and India-bound vessels (hull and machinery, cargo, P&I and war risk) with capacity of about Rs 13,000 crore. The guarantee is only a backstop for very large losses, and the aim is to reduce dependence on foreign insurers.
questions.s: Indian Infrastructure and Tribune, 12 May 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about decisions of the Union Cabinet in May 2026:
1. The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved continuation of SARTHAK-PDS for five years till 31 March 2031, with a central outlay of Rs 25,530 crore.
2. SARTHAK-PDS merges central assistance for intra-State foodgrain movement and fair price shop dealers' margin with the SMART-PDS technology reform scheme.
3. The Rs 37,500 crore scheme to promote coal and lignite gasification is administered by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The PDS scheme operates under the National Food Security Act, 2013. The gasification scheme, aimed at syngas for chemicals, fertilisers and fuels and at import substitution, is administered by the Ministry of Coal, not the Petroleum Ministry.
questions.s: IANS, The Statesman, Angel One and NBM&CW, May 2026

questions.q:
Statement-I: In mid-May 2026 India raised retail petrol and diesel prices by Rs 3 per litre and CNG by Rs 2 per kg, the first fuel price hike in more than four years.
Statement-II: Crude oil prices surged past USD 120 per barrel following the disruption of the Strait of Hormuz.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Oil marketing companies had stopped daily price revisions in April 2022, so the hike ended a long freeze. India imports most of its crude (88.2 per cent in 2024-25), so a Hormuz-driven spike in global prices flows straight into pump prices, and petrol and diesel carry a weight of nearly 5 per cent in the CPI.
questions.s: Al Jazeera and IAS Baba, 15 May 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Electronic Gold Receipts launched by the National Stock Exchange on 5 May 2026:
1. Live trading in the receipts began on 18 May 2026.
2. They are dematerialised securities backed by physical gold stored in SEBI-accredited vaults and held through depositories.
3. They are issued by the Government of India under the Sovereign Gold Bond scheme.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Electronic Gold Receipts aim to formalise the gold market and improve price discovery by letting investors hold gold electronically. They are backed by physical gold in vaults, whereas Sovereign Gold Bonds are government securities issued by the RBI on behalf of the Centre.
questions.s: ETV Bharat and All India Radio, 5 May 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the energy and foreign-exchange situation in India in May 2026:
1. The Prime Minister urged citizens at Vadodara on 11 May to save fuel, reduce consumption of foreign-made products and avoid buying gold until the West Asia crisis eases.
2. The rupee touched record lows against the US dollar in May 2026.
3. India's crude oil import dependence in 2024-25 was about 60 per cent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The appeal was aimed at conserving foreign exchange as the Iran war and Strait of Hormuz disruption raised India's import bill. India's crude oil import dependence was a record 88.2 per cent in 2024-25, much higher than 60 per cent.
questions.s: All India Radio and IAS Baba, 11 May 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Monetary Policy Committee's decision of 5 June 2026:
1. The repo rate was left unchanged at 5.25 per cent, the rate reached after a 25 basis point cut from 5.50 per cent in December 2025.
2. The decision to keep the rate unchanged was taken by a 4-2 majority.
3. The FY27 real GDP growth projection was cut to 6.6 per cent from 6.9 per cent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Committee, chaired by Governor Sanjay Malhotra, voted unanimously to hold the rate with a neutral stance, and raised its FY27 CPI inflation projection to 5.1 per cent. The MPC is a six-member statutory body with the Governor as ex-officio chairperson.
questions.s: Drishti IAS, Outlook Money and SCC Online, 5 Jun 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following measures announced by the RBI in June 2026 to support the rupee:
1. The RBI will bear the full hedging cost for authorised banks raising fresh 3-5 year FCNR(B) deposits until 30 September 2026.
2. The Fully Accessible Route was expanded to cover 15-, 30- and 40-year Government securities.
3. The period for realisation of export proceeds was lengthened from 9 months to 15 months.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: FCNR(B) deposits are held by NRIs in designated foreign currencies, so removing the hedging cost makes them cheaper for banks to raise and brings in dollars. The export-proceeds period was cut from 15 to 9 months, which forces exporters to bring foreign exchange home sooner.
questions.s: MUFG Research and SCC Online, 5 Jun 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The India-Oman Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement came into force on 1 June 2026, making Oman the second Gulf Cooperation Council member, after the UAE, with which India has a bilateral trade pact.
2. The India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement and the Double Contribution Convention are to enter into force on 15 July 2026.
3. The Double Contribution Convention reduces the exemption period from social-security contributions for posted workers from 5 years to 3 years.
4. The additional tariff of up to 12.5 per cent proposed by the US Trade Representative under a Section 301 investigation in June 2026 targets India alone.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Convention raises the exemption period from 3 to 5 years, the opposite of statement 3. The USTR proposal, on alleged failure to curb trade in goods made with forced labour, covers India and 53 other economies, so statement 4 is wrong.
questions.s: Deccan Herald, Tribune, IANS and Moneylife, Jun 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the BHAVYA portal launched on 9 June 2026 for the Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana:
1. The scheme aims to develop 500 plug-and-play industrial parks.
2. The National Industrial Corridor Development Corporation is the project management agency and partners with States through a 51:49 SPV model.
3. The minimum land requirement is 100 acres in non-hilly States and 25 acres in hilly, north-eastern and smaller States and UTs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The scheme, of about Rs 33,660 crore, covers 100 parks over six years (2026-27 to 2031-32), with up to 50 parks in the first phase. The Union Cabinet approved it on 18 March 2026.
questions.s: Drishti IAS, ITLN and Onmanorama, 9 Jun 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Coal Exchange Rules, 2026:
1. They enable market-based coal trading on a many-to-many platform, replacing the single-seller, multiple-buyer model.
2. The Coal Controller Organisation is the authority to register and regulate coal exchanges, with 25-year registrations.
3. They follow the Coal Mines (Special Provisions) Act, 2015, which introduced the concept of a Mineral Exchange.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Rules follow the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2025, which introduced the Mineral Exchange concept. Commercial and captive miners and public sector coal companies can sell on the platform.
questions.s: All India Radio and Tribune, 9 Jun 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Aviation Turbine Fuel price stabilisation arrangement approved by the Union Cabinet on 3 June 2026:
1. The support of up to Rs 10,000 crore is given as a direct cash subsidy to airlines.
2. Oil marketing companies absorb losses when the import parity price of ATF exceeds an approved benchmark, and surpluses are recovered when prices fall.
3. ATF is outside the GST regime and is taxed by States through VAT.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The one-time support takes the form of interest-free advances to oil marketing companies, not payments to airlines; participating airlines must buy ATF only from those companies for up to three years. ATF is about 40 per cent of airline operating costs, which is why price swings during the West Asia crisis hurt airlines so much.
questions.s: Onmanorama, UNI and Drishti IAS, 3 Jun 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the new Wholesale Price Index series released on 15 June 2026:
1. The series has base year 2022-23, replacing 2011-12, and expands the item basket from 697 to 957.
2. Items are weighted by Gross Value of Output rather than net traded value.
3. Crude petroleum and natural gas are moved from Fuel and Power to Primary Articles.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The change goes the other way: crude petroleum and natural gas move from Primary Articles to Fuel and Power. The new WPI will run for five years before being discontinued in favour of Producer Price Indices, and all-commodities WPI inflation for May 2026 was 9.68 per cent.
questions.s: Drishti IAS, Office of the Economic Adviser (DPIIT) and Moneylife, 15 Jun 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the RBI's Upper Layer NBFC classification directions issued on 24 June 2026:
1. NBFCs with assets of Rs 1 lakh crore or more in their latest audited balance sheet fall in the Upper Layer, replacing the earlier parametric scoring method.
2. The asset threshold is reviewed every five years.
3. NBFCs in the Upper Layer must list on stock exchanges within three years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The threshold is reviewed every three years, not five. The listing requirement revived the debate over Tata Sons, an Upper Layer NBFC-CIC since September 2022, which has sought deregistration; 15 NBFCs had been identified in the Upper Layer so far.
questions.s: Business Today and Moneylife, 24 Jun 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana:
1. The scheme has an outlay of Rs 99,446 crore and came into effect on 1 August 2025.
2. Employers receive up to Rs 15,000 per month for each additional employee.
3. First-time employees receive up to Rs 15,000.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Employers receive up to Rs 3,000 per month for each additional employee, and manufacturing employers get incentives for four years. On 19 June 2026 the Prime Minister disbursed about Rs 2,400 crore to more than 15 lakh persons, the first large payout under the Employment Linked Incentive scheme, which targets over 3.5 crore jobs over two years.
questions.s: All India Radio and PM India, 19 Jun 2026
